current.title: Open problem: Fluctuation exponent of directed polymers beyond the logarithmic improvement
current.body:
OPEN PROBLEM (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status attempted_unsolved). Improve the bound Var(log Z_n) = O(n/log n) for directed polymers in random environment in general dimension to a power improvement n^{1-eps}. Source: Chatterjee: Chaos, concentration and multiple valleys, 2008, with open questions, Section 12, problem (3), p. 59. Status notes: In d = 1+1 with exactly solvable weights (log-gamma, exponential last-passage) the exponent 2/3 (variance n^{2/3}) is a theorem; for general weights in any dimension the BKS-type n/log n remains the best general bound to this session's knowledge; cf. the FPP variance problem in the Codex campaign (P-a/ chi = 1/3 target).
Posed in Chatterjee: Chaos, concentration and multiple valleys, 2008, with open questions
Current status unverified as of 2026-09-07

corrected.title: Open problem: Fluctuation exponent of directed polymers beyond the logarithmic improvement
corrected.statement: OPEN PROBLEM (historically listed in 2008; current openness UNKNOWN). Let M_n be the maximum sum of iid standard Gaussian vertex weights over up-right n-vertex paths from the origin in Z^2, with a free endpoint. The cited source proves Var(M_n)<=C n/log n. The task strengthening asks for constants epsilon in (0,1) and C<infinity independent of n such that Var(M_n)<=C n^(1-epsilon) for all n>=2. No such power improvement is established in this packet. Positive-temperature log partition functions, general disorder and higher dimensions require separate sources and are not identified with this cited ground-state model.
